claim: Systemic bias is not merely dirt in an otherwise neutral data stream.
scene: Begin with a simple diagram of a straight, white data stream flowing through a pipeline. Add three overlay layers one by one: (1) a building icon labeled "Historical Institutions" with an arrow feeding subtle color tints into the stream; (2) a server rack icon labeled "Digital Infrastructure" injecting patterned noise; (3) a bullseye icon labeled "Statistical Objectives" adding weighting spikes. Each arrow is annotated "bias injection point". After the three steps, the stream is now a multicolored, uneven flow, illustrating that bias is woven into the data by these relationships, not just surface dirt. A side‑by‑side split‑screen compares the original clean line to the biased line, reinforcing why the statement holds.
